Oh, and Derrick Henry will look to run all over his former team in the Tennessee Titans . That's a must-watch revenge game. Let's discuss some anytime touchdown bets. These have become popular wagers among football fans because of their longer odds. Even when it comes to an expected TD scorer, they make for a fun parlay leg. Last week, we hit on Tee Higgins at +175 and tight end Harold Fannin Jr . at +235. Let's see what we have cooking up for Week 4. Below, we will break down five anytime TD bets to consider. These will not be predictable choices like a Jahmyr Gibbs or Bijan Robinson score that offer zero value, but they won't be wild long shots such as a team defense. Let's begin with a tight end who looked incredible last week in his 2026 debut. Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook. 1. Raiders TE Brock Bowers (+160) The Las Vegas Raiders have a massive matchup against Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs this week. The Raiders are off to a surprising 3-0 start, although we can't ignore the fact that they've played the easiest strength of schedule in the NFL up to this point, as their first three opponents have won one game combined. Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers made his season debut last week against the New Orleans Saints , and he looked magnificent. He caught a game-high 10 passes for 116 yards and a touchdown in a 35-27 win, and will be important if the Raiders want to score an upset victory over their rivals. With how good Bowers looked last week, I'll sprinkle on him again in this spot as Kirk Cousins ' new clear-cut "WR1." 2. Bills RB James Cook (-140) James Cook of the Buffalo Bills is one of the best running backs in the NFL, and he's on a bit of a heater right now. He rushed 21 times for 135 yards and a touchdown in Week 2 vs. the Detroit Lions , and then 24 times for 154 yards and another touchdown last week against the Los Angeles Chargers . Now, the flailing New England Patriots come to town, and they are missing two important defenders in Christian Barmore and Christian Gonzalez . They lost by 29 points to the Jacksonville Jaguars last week, and I'm sure Joe Brady and the Bills want to do something similar to the team that won their division last year. A -140 price isn't value, but I can tell you I was surprised by this listing. 3. Vikings RB Aaron Jones (-160) Like James Cook, this line doesn't offer much value. But consider that the Miami Dolphins have allowed six touchdowns to running backs through three games. The Minnesota Vikings are favored by double-digits over Miami, which makes sense because the Dolphins just lost De'Von Achane for the year, while Brian Flores is going to look to DESTROY his former team from a defensive standpoint. That means Aaron Jones is going to get plenty of touches. He hasn't scored since Week 1, but will in Week 4. 4. Jets RB Braelon Allen (+115) I was a fan of Braelon Allen in the 2024 draft process because he's big at 6-foot-1, 235 pounds, and was the youngest player in the entire class. He actually racked up 482 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns as a rookie, but an injury held him to four games played last year. Now, he's making his third career start with Breece Hall sidelined by a quad injury. When the New York Jets get in the red zone against the Chicago Bears , Frank Reich is going to call his number. 5. Saints RB Alvin Kamara (+135) (Monday) This game is on Monday night, but I had to mention it. The Saints are hosting the Atlanta Falcons in the 20th anniversary of the "Rebirth Game," where the Saints returned to the Superdome for the first time following Hurricane Katrina. The legendary Steve Gleason blocked a punt on the opening drive of the game, which set the tone for an emotional 23-3 Saints victory. I can't imagine what the environment will be like on Monday night. Travis Etienne is out with a hamstring injury, opening the door for franchise legend Alvin Kamara . He's not as productive as he used to be, but it makes too much sense for him to score in this game. Bonus: Ravens RB Derrick Henry 2 TDs (+250) Derrick Henry faces the team that selected him No. 45 overall in the 2016 NFL Draft this Sunday. Henry and the Titans didn't have some dramatic breakup, but Henry wanted to win football games and the Titans were about to suffer an embarrassing fall to the bottom of the league, so a mutual parting of ways made sense. It used to be a debate if Henry was a future Hall of Famer. Not anymore. The ageless wonder leads the NFL with 3,817 rushing yards and 38 rushing touchdowns since signing with the Baltimore Ravens in 2024. Those are more rushing yards and more rushing touchdowns than the entire Titans offense since he left. Derrick Henry to find the end zone at -210 is probably a parlay leg, but what about two touchdowns at +250? He's averaging two touchdowns a game this year as it is! They also placed both starting cornerbacks on IR, so things could be dicey against this explosive Lions offense. Get a $55 bonus after $25 in trades by claiming the latest Kalshi promo code CBSSPORTS55 here : Best bets for Sunday Night Football Over 51.5 This line has climbed a full point over the last 24 hours, and that probably involves the weather. The Lions' last appearance in prime time cashed everyone out with the explosive matchup against the Bills . I'm not expecting Carolina to perform like Buffalo did, but the Panthers are highly susceptible to being dragged into shootouts if their opponent starts to sling the ball around. Given the dearth of defensive backfield talent out there for Carolina, I fully expect the Lions to take advantage and throw the ball downfield. Carolina should be able to answer and we should get points galore. He broke out in Week 2 with a pair of scores then was rewarded with eight targets in Week 3 against the Browns . I'd expect him to see close to that many again Sunday night, making this number just way too low for how much Bryce looks his way, especially if Jalen Coker ends up inactive tonight. But he's been just OK thus far, and as such we're getting a great price. Jamo can score from anywhere, should get plenty of short-yardage looks with screens and the like and also is the ultimate deep threat going against a really depleted secondary. Brycen Tremayne (+360, DraftKings) This is a bit of a longshot, but, again, we're thinking Jalen Coker won't play in this game. That's going to likely slide Tremayne into a starting role opposite of Tetairoa McMillan at wide receiver, and if this is a shootout, Young is going to have to throw a lot. There's a good chance Tremayne gets lost in the sauce near the end zone, setting him up as a nice high-value play to score. MORE: Check out our Pro Picks page for NFL best bets from all of our analysts Indianapolis Colts vs. Washington Commanders – 9:30 am ET (London) The Colts might be down Alec Pierce, but I like the way this offense operates. Indianapolis lost a tough one in Kansas City two weeks ago, but the team put up 30 points against a Chiefs team that is sixth in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (-0.077) this year. It’s just hard to stop the Colts once Jonathan Taylor gets going on the ground. He puts Indianapolis in a ton of manageable third-and-short situations. Of course, Washington is a top-five team in Rush EPA/Play Allowed (-0.318) right now. The Commanders have done a good job of stuffing opponents thus far. But they haven’t seen an offensive line quite like this, and they haven’t faced a running back this efficient. Also, if Washington is selling out to stop the run, Daniel Jones should be able to do some real damage through the air — especially when looking Josh Downs’ way. I also happen to love the Commanders to put up points on the Colts defense. Marcus Mariota is an excellent backup, so Washington’s offense isn’t going to completely stall out with Jayden Daniels injured. Mariota played well in relief of Daniels two games ago, and he threw for three touchdowns in his start last week. He’s accurate, he understands the offense, and he’s still a threat with his legs. He’s also up against a Colts defense that is 30th in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (0.124). Honestly, this might not seem like the most enticing standalone game, but I think it’s going to deliver some early-morning excitement. Two shaky defenses should mean a real shot at a shootout. Also, since 2024, the Over is 15-1 when Washington is an underdog of 3.5 to 9.5 points. The average total points scored in such games is 58.2 points per game. Bet: Over 46.5 (-115) Dallas Cowboys at Houston Texans – 1:00 pm ET We haven’t seen anything from Houston this season, but a bounce-back performance should be coming soon. I don’t expect the Texans to completely stifle a good Cowboys offense, but I do know that Houston is much better than its No. 19 ranking in EPA/Play Allowed (0.012) this year. This is a Texans defense that has been elite for years, and none of the moves made in the offseason should have resulted in this type of drop-off. That said, look for Houston to start playing some much better defense, and we could see it start with a decent showing against Dak Prescott and Co. I also love any offense in a matchup with the Cowboys defense, as Dallas is at the bottom of the league in EPA/Play Allowed (0.193). The Cowboys made some moves to address their miserable defense from last season, but it doesn’t look like any of them have worked. So, this should be a pretty strong matchup for CJ Stroud. Of course, Stroud has issues as a passer, but he’s reliable when he has time to get his feet set. That’s a good thing as Stroud prepares to face a defense that is 31st in Pass Rush Win Rate (40%). He should have plenty of time. This is also a massive desperation spot for Houston. I can’t imagine Dallas is thrilled to be sitting at 1-2 right now, but Houston’s season might be over if the team drops this one to fall to 0-4. This season, the Cardinals are allowing 247.0 passing yards per game, and their two starting corners have an average PFF grade of 52.1. New York has been conservative with Winston so far, opting to lean heavily into a ground-and-pound approach. However, the Giants need to play the matchup, and this is one that calls for some passing. Arizona is a top-10 team in pass frequency. So, if the Cardinals are letting Jacoby Brissett air it out, the Giants will have no choice but to let Winston do the same. I know Winston hasn’t yet thrown for a score, and he also hasn’t eclipsed 118 passing yards in a game. But we all know that Winston is a gunslinger, and you don’t have to go back too far to find a box score in which he threw for 366 yards and two touchdowns. That was November 23, 2025, when Winston got involved in a shootout with the Lions. Rueben Bain Jr. to be a Top 10 pick: Yes ( -162 ) “Miami Hurricanes EDGE Rueben Bain Jr. has 30.9-inch arms, which likely cause him to slide, but I don't think he can get past eight overall to the New Orleans Saints or nine overall to the Kansas City Chiefs. The 21-year-old finished fifth in the ACC with 7.5 sacks as a freshman, before regressing somewhat as a sophomore while battling injuries. Bain Jr. then returned to form this past year, setting career-highs in tackles (54), tackles for loss (15.5), and sacks (9.5), while leading the Hurricanes to a College Football Playoff (CFP) National Championship appearance. This earned him AP Consensus All-America and ACC Defensive Player of the Year honors, as well as the Ted Hendricks Award. Those accomplishments, a high character, and elite film should be enough to keep him inside the top 10 picks, making this arguably the best prop bet available.” – Seth Woolcock ( FantasyPros ) Jacob Rodriguez drafted inside the top-32 ( +500 ) “I’m a sucker for the “Will this player be drafted in Round 1″ betting market. Right now, my favorite approach is to select Texas Tech LB Jacob Rodriguez inside the top-32 at 5-1 odds. He’s been a buzzy late 1st-round pick across several sources (Tony Pauline) and has been tied to several teams between picks 15-32, such as Dallas, Houston, Miami, Buffalo, Pittsburgh, Tampa Bay, New England, and Chicago.” – Andrew Erickson ( FantasyPros ) Who will be the fourth overall pick? “Arvell Reese ( +650 at DraftKings ) or Sonny Styles ( +175 at BetMGM ) — The info/draft rumors I hear about change literally by the minute. By the time you read this, things might be drastically different, but here goes nothing. (FYI- at the time of this writing, it’s Wednesday night, 10:30 p.m.) Anyway, it sounds like Arizona’s owner, Michael Bidwell, might veto GM Monte Ossenfort’s wishes to trade out of the third pick. The rumor is that Ossenfort apparently either wants Edge David Bailey if he’s there or to trade it for more picks if the Jets select Bailey. However, Bidwell wants Jeremiyah Love because he would add some excitement to the Cardinals’ fan base and could help sell some tickets. So, if you think Arizona keeps the pick and selects Love, I think the best way to play that would be to bet the Titans to select Arvell Reese and Sonny Styles. I don’t think Titans’ head coach Robert Saleh (who is a former defensive coordinator) would take Love, Carnell Tate, or Jordyn Tyson over a good prospect on defense, even if he slips. And if Arizona picks Love, you essentially get a free roll with Reese, assuming the Titans don’t trade the pick. Worth a shot.” – Mark Ringo ( Sleepers and Busts ) Carnell Tate drafted in Top 7 ( +105 ) “Carnell Tate’s draft position u7.5 ( +105 at DraftKings ). I’m surprised this bet hasn’t been steamed, but it could be by the time you read this. I’ll grab this bet and take it anywhere I can find it for plus money. Tate’s floor right now looks like seventh overall to the Commanders, and I wouldn’t be shocked if he went as high as fourth overall to the Titans.” – Derek Brown ( FantasyPros ) Fewer than 8.5 SEC players drafted in First Round ( -185 ) “You’ll make money if you bet that there will be fewer than 8.5 players from SEC schools selected in the first round (-185). Normally, the first round of the draft is littered with SEC guys. Not this year. Mansoor Delane (LSU), Kadyn Proctor (Alabama), and Keldric Faulk (Auburn) are the SEC’s only first-round locks, and K.C. Concepcion (Texas A&M) is a near-lock. That’s four. Jermod McCoy (Tennessee), Colton Hood (Tennessee), and Ty Simpson (Alabama) are better than 50/50 to go in the first round, but McCoy’s stock is plummeting due to a worrisome knee issue, and there are only two or three potential first-round suitors for Simpson, none of whom would draft him with the picks they currently hold in the top half of the round. If all of these SEC maybes make it, that’s seven, leaving one SEC player to spare. Chase Bisontis (Texas A&M), Cashius Howell (Texas A&M), Zion Young (Missouri), C.J. Allen (Georgia, and Caleb Banks (Florida) are first-round possibilities. There’s a decent chance one of these players makes it into the first round. I don’t think we’ll see two or more players from this group make it, and if we do get more than one, it could very well be at the expense of McCoy, Hood, or Simpson.” – Pat Fitzmaurice ( FantasyPros ) Carnell Tate to be first WR drafted ( -180 ) “Carnell Tate is the betting favorite to be the first wide receiver selected in the 2026 NFL Draft at -180 odds, largely due to his exceptional route running and ‘pro-ready’ profile. While Jordyn Tyson is hands down the best pure receiver in this class, his extensive injury history, including major knee surgery and a broken collarbone, has dropped him to the second or third receiver off the board on most teams’ lists. NFL front offices are notoriously risk-averse in the top ten, making Tate the safer bet to anchor a professional offense immediately. This shift in draft stock highlights a classic case where reliability outweighs elite but fragile potential. Ultimately, taking Tate at these odds is a play on the certainty of his health and polished Buckeye pedigree over the medical gamble Tyson presents.” – Lawrence Iacona ( Gridiron Experts ) Makai Lemon to be first WR drafted ( +2000 ) “Makai Lemon – 1st Wide Receiver Drafted ( +2000 at Caesars ). I'm going with Makai Lemon as the first wide receiver off the board. Bold, absolutely. Crazy? Maybe, but hear me out. This is often a copycat league. I believe a wide receiver-needy team, such as the New York Giants, might consider Lemon. The Giants already have Malik Nabers, a top outside threat, and could look to replicate what Seattle did with Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Detroit with Amon-Ra St. Brown, using Lemon in a similar role. If you haven't already placed a few bets on player props, now is your chance. In this article, I'm going to give you a few of our favorites that we've written about throughout the week. Best NFL Prop Bets Today Geno Smith OVER 21.5 Completions (+103) via Caesars David Montgomery OVER 10.5 Receiving Yards (-117) via DraftKings Bryce Young OVER 249.5 Passing Yards (-111) via DraftKings Geno Smith OVER 21.5 Completions (+103) In this week' edition of the Player Prop Countdown, I ranked Geno Smith going over 21.1 completions as my No. 4-ranked prop for Week 4: Geno Smith has been impressive to start the season, despite the Jets being 1-2 through the first three weeks.

Bryce Young OVER 249.5 Passing Yards (-111) If you're looking for a prop bet for Sunday Night Football, Peter Dewey wrote in his Lions vs. Panthers player prop story why he's backing Bryce Young to have a big game: I love this line for Carolina quarterback Bryce Young, who has thrown for over 250 yards in each of his first three games this season. Young has 361, 287, and 291 yards in his three games, and Carolina is 13th in the NFL in EPA/Pass. Young has attempted at least 36 passes in each game, and he may need to throw the ball a ton against a high-powered Lions offense that has scored 31 points in every game in 2026. The Lions’ defense has struggled against the pass (27th in EPA/Pass), so Dave Canales’ offense should look to the air in Week 4. No team in the NFL has allowed more passing yards than Detroit (898), and Young has easily cleared this total even in a loss to Cleveland. I’m buying the former No. 1 overall pick, as he looks to have turned a corner a bit in his fourth NFL season.

In fact, he leads all quarterbacks in completion percentage over expected at +10.9%. He had a slow Week 1, but completed 27 passes for 247 yards against the Packers and 31 passes for 321 yards against the Lions. Let's bet on that trend to continue against the Bears. David Montgomery OVER 10.5 Receiving Yards (-117) In his props article for Cowboys vs. Texans, Ryan Gilbert broke down why he likes David Montgomery to go over his receiving yards total of 10.5: David Montgomery is being used in the passing game a bit more in Houston than he was in Detroit, where Jahmyr Gibbs was the main back there. The veteran has caught all seven of his targets this season for 48 yards, going OVER 10.5 in all three games. Montgomery isn’t going to get a ton of targets, but he’s caught multiple passes in each game thus far, with 19, 14, and 15 receiving yards. I expect him to keep that going against this Cowboys defense that allowed 40 receiving yards to Rachaad White two weeks ago.

highlights: Player Prop Countdown: Top 10 NFL Player Props for Week 4 We're now three weeks into the NFL season, which means we have a solid base of statistics and metrics to lean on when placing our bets. Best NFL Week 4 Prop Bets 10) Ollie Gordon II UNDER 21.5 Rush Yards (-115) via Caesars With De'Von Achane now out for the season after suffering an ACL injury last week, fantasy owners and bettors alike were scrambling to get a piece of Ollie Gordon II. Unfortunately for those who did, the Dolphins' true No. 2 back, Jaylen Wright, is on his way to returning to the field this week. If that happens, Gordon's carries may be limited.

The fact that he's playing the Texans this week may give you some pause to bet the OVER on his passing yards total, but let's remember that Houston's defense looks like a shell of its former self in 2026. Let's back Prescott on Sunday. 6) Jonathan Taylor UNDER 89.5 Rush Yards (+100) via TheScore Bet Age may be catching up to Jonathan Taylor. Now, he has to face a Commanders team that has been solid at stopping the run this season, giving up just 3.8 yards per rush, third in opponent rush EPA, and sixth in opponent rush success rate. It's a bold move, but I'm ready to fade the Colts' running back. 5) Michael Wilson Anytime Touchdown (+210) via FanDuel

He and the rest of the Cardinals now get to face a Giants defense that ranks 27th in opponent dropback EPA and 23rd in opponent dropback success rate. That could lead to big things for the Arizona wide receiver. 4) Geno Smith OVER 21.5 Completions (+103) via Caesars Geno Smith has been impressive to start the season, despite the Jets being 1-2 through the first three weeks. In fact, he leads all quarterbacks in completion percentage over expected at +10.9%. He had a slow Week 1, but completed 27 passes for 247 yards against the Packers and 31 passes for 321 yards against the Lions. Let's bet on that trend to continue against the Bears.

An NFL player prop is a bet on how an individual player will perform in a game. Instead of betting on the winner, point spread, or total score, you're betting on a specific outcome or statistic for that player. Common NFL player props include: Passing yards, completions, attempts, and passing touchdowns (quarterbacks). Rushing yards and rushing attempts (running backs, quarterbacks, and other rushers). Receptions and receiving yards (wide receivers, tight ends, and running backs). Anytime, first, and multiple touchdown scorers (eligible offensive players and defenses/special teams). Most player props are offered as over/under bets. For example, a sportsbook might set a quarterback's passing yards at 245.5. You can bet the over if you think he'll finish with 246 or more, or the under if you think he'll finish with 245 or fewer. Touchdown scorer props work differently: you’re simply betting whether a player scores, with the odds reflecting the sportsbook's assessment of how likely that is. One thing that makes player props different from game bets is how much they depend on the game script. A team that falls behind by three scores is likely to throw more and run less, which can boost passing and receiving opportunities while cutting into rushing volume. That's why our projections account for the expected game script when estimating how a player is likely to perform. From projection to probability : We run simulations of the upcoming game to estimate how often a player finishes over or under the specific line being offered. That gives us the probability shown on the board. Probability meets price : We compare our projected probability with the probability implied by the sportsbook's odds.
